<!-- B"H
Boruch Hashem
Blessed is He

The Awtsmoos reveals another layer after deployment: a server may be healthy while its paid-provider vessel is not yet filled;
Awtsmoos.com should therefore reveal provider readiness before the user spends intention, so absence becomes guidance instead of a failed-history field.
-->

# Connection Readiness Continuation

## Observed production secret topology

- `awtsmoos.service` fragment: `/etc/systemd/system/awtsmoos.service`.
- Immutable release drop-in: `/etc/systemd/system/awtsmoos.service.d/10-immutable-release.conf`.
- `EnvironmentFiles` is empty.
- Live service process does not contain the `MINIMAX_API_KEY` environment name.
- `/etc/environment` is readable but contains no MiniMax environment variable name.
- The immutable-release drop-in contains no MiniMax environment variable name.
- No credential value was printed or inspected.

Conclusion: there is no existing production MiniMax credential available through the discovered service/environment path. The credential boundary remains genuinely external.

## Newly discovered UX gap

The application already fetches safe connection state into `AppShell.connection`, but `AppViews` passes connection state only to Settings. Create therefore evaluates draft/media readiness without provider readiness. A user can write a valid prompt and receive an enabled Generate button even though production already knows that MiniMax is not configured.

## Improvement plan

1. Add a small provider-readiness domain object that combines draft readiness with the safe proxy status.
2. Pass `AppShell.connection` into Create view state.
3. Render a compact provider-status banner in Create when the server key is unavailable or the status check failed.
4. Disable Generate whenever either draft readiness or provider readiness is false.
5. Make the readiness message distinguish creative requirements from server configuration requirements.
6. Add a direct Settings action from the provider-status banner.
7. Add a second programmatic guard in `ComposerActions.generate()` so UI state cannot be bypassed.
8. Refresh connection status on browser `online` events and when the user returns to Create, without polling aggressively.
9. Add focused tests for configured, unconfigured, and status-error states.
10. Re-run local/browser gates, then publish as an isolated fast-forward patch release from current `origin/main`.

## Release safety

The original shared worktree remains dirty with unrelated work. This patch must again be released from an isolated clean worktree based on the then-current `origin/main`, copying only whole changed Olam files.

## NEXT_ACTION

Read the exact Create renderer/controller callback contracts, then rewrite provider-readiness modules and bindings as complete files.
